text: The Zekhring[1] are from the Anjaw District (formerly part of Lohit district) of Arunachal Pradesh. They live in the hilly terrain and banks of the Lohit River in the Walong and Kibithoo area. They are Animists, although they have recently co-adopted Tibetan Buddhism. [2] The Zekhring sustain their livelihoods through agriculture. text: Zakhring is an endangered indigenous language of China. It belongs to the Sino-Tibetan language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by adults only. It is not known to be taught in schools.
